testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

unverified.claim: When `review <pr> --result <path>` replays a result the PR's rows already carry and also gets a new launch token in the same call, the receipt still names that result as `reviewed` and has no `written: false`. A reader therefore cannot tell from the receipt that the reviewed= was skipped and only the launch was written.
unverified.evidence: probe/t4.sh: I seeded `#99 review=member:review-pr-99`, then ran `review 99 --result …/pr99/run-abcdefgh/review.json --scratch $S` (writes the token). I then ran `review 99 review=member:review-pr-99-b --result …/run-abcdefgh/review.json --scratch $S`. It printed `review on row #99` and the receipt `{"pr":99,…,"line":"#99 review=member:review-pr-99 · reviewed=aaaaaaa:1/0/0:run-abcdefgh · review=member:review-pr-99-b","created":false,"reviewed":"reviewed=aaaaaaa:1/0/0:run-abcdefgh","next":"review-pr-99-c"}`, exit 0. The reviewed= was not appended again, but the receipt reads as if it was. Impact is low: the only code caller (fleet-event.mjs:877) never passes launch tokens alongside --result.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add `reviewed` to the receipt only when it was actually appended, or always add a `written` boolean for the reviewed= (true or false) next to `reviewed`.

unverified.claim: The spec table still says the `review-result` wake 'reads the digest, `ledger.mjs review <pr> reviewed=<head>:<s>/<r>/<u>:<run>`'. After this PR, that exact call is refused at exit 2.
unverified.evidence: grep across plugin/docs/tests for `review \S+ reviewed=` found only this line among docs that are not fixtures. probe/t2.sh: `ledger.mjs review 99 "review=member:review-pr-99-b reviewed=aaaaaaa:1/0/0:run-abcdefgh"` → `ledger: review #99: 'reviewed=…' is a reviewed= token — a reviewed= is a Gate verdict, written only with `ledger.mjs review 99 --result <path>`…`, exit=2.
unverified.suggested_fix: If dated specs are kept current in this repo, change the row to `ledger.mjs review <pr> --result <path> --scratch <scratch>`. Otherwise leave it as a historical record.

unverified.claim: Two refusals name different writers for the same token: gateVerdictWriter() names `fleet-event.mjs review-result <pr> <path>` for a malformed reviewed=, while reviewTokenWriter() in ledger.mjs names `ledger.mjs review <pr> --result <path>`. Both commands work, but the operator sees two different 'only writer' answers.
unverified.evidence: Read ledger-grammar.mjs:456-462 (gateVerdictWriter) and ledger.mjs:3121-3125 (reviewTokenWriter). probe/t2.sh `row 99 "#99 … reviewed=…"` printed the ledger.mjs form: `adds review token 'reviewed=…' — a reviewed= is written only with `ledger.mjs review <pr> --result <path>`…`. I did not execute the gateVerdictWriter path (it needs a malformed reviewed= word that passes the review-token check first).
unverified.suggested_fix: Make both messages name one writer, for example `ledger.mjs review <pr> --result <path>` (via `fleet-event.mjs review-result`).

unverified.claim: reviewResult swallows a JSON.parse failure on the ledger's stdout with an empty catch. When the receipt is unreadable it reports `PR #n the result at <path>` as if the token had been written, with no stderr signal and exit 0. It also cannot tell a fresh write from `written:false`.
unverified.evidence: In the copy I made `ledger.mjs review` print `junk` instead of its JSON receipt, then ran `node --test --test-name-pattern='review-result hands' tests/fleet-event.test.mjs`. The run exited 0 with the event line `event: review-result: PR #88 the result at /…/pr88/run-abcdefgh/review.json`. The expected `PR #88 reviewed=…` did not appear, so the summary line asserts a write the code never confirmed.
unverified.suggested_fix: Treat an unparseable receipt after exit 0 as a refusal: call ev.refuse, or at least print a stderr line. Do not fall back to `written !== false` meaning "written".

unverified.claim: The pr cross-check `result?.pr !== undefined && Number(result.pr) !== pr` is the only content check on the file's PR, and it silently passes when `pr` is missing. It also passes a `pr` that Number() coerces to the PR number, such as `[482]` or `"0x1e2"`. `ledger.mjs review --result` is now the sole writer of the `reviewed=` Gate verdict, so this guard is the thing standing between a mislabelled file and a verdict.
unverified.evidence: In a scratch ledger with `#1 impl-1=PR#482 → PR#482 · review=member:review-pr-482`, I wrote review.json under `<scratch>/pr482/run-Aa11Bb22/` with each of these `pr` values: absent, `[482]`, `"0x1e2"`. All three exited 0 and wrote `reviewed=aaaaaaa:1/2/3:run-Aa11Bb22`. A file with `counts.survived:"x"` and a file containing `null` were refused with the "carries no head and counts" message, so those paths do fail loudly. The path partition still binds the PR, so this is a weakened check, not a bypass.
unverified.suggested_fix: Require `result.pr` to be present and `Number.isInteger(result.pr) && result.pr === pr` (or a strict string compare), and die otherwise.

unverified.claim: The `real()` helper returns the lexical path on any realpathSync error, not only ENOENT. EACCES and ELOOP on the partition or run root silently weaken the partition check to a string comparison. The PR moved this helper from fleet-event.mjs into ledger.mjs, where it now guards the Gate verdict.
unverified.evidence: Read from the diff only; I did not exercise the EACCES or ELOOP path. The `catch {}` has no error-code filter.
unverified.suggested_fix: Fall back only when `e.code === "ENOENT"`; otherwise die with the error.

unverified.claim: PR body: 'a head under seven digits' is loose, since REVIEWED needs 7 to 40 hex characters rather than digits. The other body claims I checked match the code: the `--result`/`--scratch` flags, the refusal messages, the `written: false` receipt, review-eval dropping `ledger`, the runner body edit, and fleet-event's own path checks being removed.
unverified.evidence: ledger-grammar.mjs:246 holds `REVIEWED = /^reviewed=([0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}):(\d+)\/(\d+)\/(\d+):(run-[A-Za-z0-9]{8})$/`. The body's acceptance message matches the diff's `reviewed= token` die text.

unverified.claim: The writer policy for review tokens (`reviewed=` only from `review --result`, `review=` launches by argument) is enforced by runtime string-prefix checks (`startsWith`, `isReviewToken`, `reviewTokenWriter`), not by distinct types. The token is a bare string, so a caller can pass any string.
unverified.evidence: Read the diff: runReview rejects typed `reviewed=` arguments with die(), and tokenRefusal uses reviewTokenWriter(tok) to name the writer. This is consistent with the repo's untyped-JS style. I ran no probe, so I did not test it for bypass.
unverified.suggested_fix: None needed in plain JS. Keep the refusals centralized in the grammar module, as they are.

unverified.claim: runReview's flag loop checks the token twice: once against the bare flags (`word !== "--result" && word !== "--scratch"`) and then against the `=` forms with startsWith, and it computes `word.split("=")[0]` twice inside the error message. Splitting the word once gives one check with the same behavior.
unverified.evidence: Probe simplify/probe.mjs compared the current classifier with the simplified one on 19 inputs (--result, --scratch, --result=, --result=x, --scratch=a=b, --resultx, --results=1, --scratchy, review=…, review=…=failed, reviewed=…, '', '=', '--', '-result', '--RESULT=x', 'review=--result=x', …): `classifier equivalent over 19 inputs: true`. With the edit applied in my copy, the six affected test files passed 578/578, including ledger-row-review.test.mjs:632 `refusedCall(["review","482",`--result=${path}`],[/space-separated value/])`.

unverified.claim: REVIEWED_WORD is a byte-for-byte copy of ledger-grammar.mjs's exported REVIEWED regex. If the grammar changes, the test helper's copy can drift from it; importing REVIEWED removes the copy.
unverified.evidence: Probe: `REVIEWED_WORD identical to REVIEWED: true` (same .source and .flags; ledger-grammar.mjs:246). In my copy, swapping in `import { REVIEWED as REVIEWED_WORD } from "../../plugin/scripts/ledger-grammar.mjs"` kept all 578 targeted tests passing (tap: # pass 578, # fail 0).
unverified.suggested_fix: Delete the local regex and `import { REVIEWED } from "../../plugin/scripts/ledger-grammar.mjs";`. Other support files already import from plugin/scripts; for example, dispositions-fixture.mjs imports label-map.mjs.

unverified.claim: writeReviewResult's `extra = {}` parameter and its `...extra` spread are never used, and the function's `export` has no importer: viaResult is the only caller, and it passes three arguments.
unverified.evidence: grep -rn 'writeReviewResult\|viaResult' tests (excluding the helper itself) found only `viaResult` imports and calls: ledger-row-review:30/63, ledger-dispatch:25/66, ledger-settle-report:25/99, dispositions-fixture:20/136, dispositions-check:25/121, ledger-rotate:26/74. Nothing outside the helper imports writeReviewResult. With `extra` and the export removed in my copy, the 578 targeted tests passed.
unverified.suggested_fix: `function writeReviewResult(scratch, pr, token) {` with no export, and drop `...extra,` from the JSON object.

unverified.claim: The review-result test sets `const call = `ledger review 88 --result ${path} --scratch ${f.scratch}`` at line 1432, then types out the same template literal again for the second run's expected order instead of reusing `call`.
unverified.evidence: grep in the snapshot: line 1432 `const call = `ledger review 88 --result ${path} --scratch ${f.scratch}`;` and line 1442 `assert.deepEqual(second.order, [`ledger review 88 --result ${path} --scratch ${f.scratch}`, TICK]);`. unverified.claim: After this PR deleted the `const { survived, refuted, unverified } = result.counts` destructure, the counts-guard comment's reason is out of date. It says a result with no counts 'would otherwise throw on the destructure below', but no destructure is left: digestOf only reads `result[k]`. The guard should stay because removing it would change behavior, but its comment should give the reason it still has.
unverified.evidence: `grep -n 'const {[^}]*} = result\|result.counts' plugin/scripts/review-eval.mjs` → only line 190 (the comment) and line 199 (the guard). review-core.mjs:900-901 `digestOf(result) { return Object.fromEntries(DIGEST_KEYS.map((k) => [k, result[k]])); }` does not destructure counts. pr.diff shows the destructure removed at the old line 234. Mainly a comment-accuracy issue, filed here because the PR's simplification caused it.
unverified.suggested_fix: Reword the comment's reason, for example: a result with no object `counts` has no counts for the digest and nothing `ledger.mjs review --result` could derive a reviewed= from, so it is treated as an empty return. Keep the guard.
